title: Why leopards take dinner up a tree

scenes.headline: Why do leopards drag dinner up a tree?
To keep it away from thieves
scenes.body: Spotted hyenas steal leopard kills. Kills left on the ground were more likely to be stolen.

scenes.label: of kills were hoisted into trees
scenes.source: Balme et al. 2017, Journal of Animal Ecology

scenes.headline: After the hunt: a long groom
scenes.body: This male is cleaning his fur after catching a warthog. No carcass in shot.

scenes.headline: Lost meals cost cubs
scenes.body: Females that lost more kills to thieves raised fewer young each year.

caption:
A tree is a leopard's fridge with a lock on it.

In the same study, at least 21% of kills were stolen, mostly by spotted hyenas, and the risk was highest for big kills left on the ground.

Source: Balme, Miller, Pitman & Hunter 2017, Journal of Animal Ecology. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Predation told through behaviour and a peer-reviewed number, with no kill on screen (grooming after, not the carcass). HIGH-RISK format with third-party footage; only OK as a series with our own footage.
